newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says 4th ENI offer in 6 mos or more.
newsitem.headline: Italy says 4th ENI offer in 6 mos or more.

text.p: The Italian Treasury on Thursday said it would not make another offer of ENI shares until at least six months after its June third tranche sale.
Treasury Director General Mario Draghi was speaking at a news conference where he announced that the energy company's third tranche sale would take place from June 23-27.
"The lock-up period is for 180 days, against the 270 days the last time," Draghi said.
The Treasury sold some 16 percent of ENI shares last October after a first tranche sale of 15 percent in November 1995.

As with the previous offer, the third tranche sale will go to the Italian public, ENI employees and Italian and foreign institutional investors. ENI is the world's sixth-largest energy company and Italy's biggest company by stock market capitalisation,
A series of roadshows in Europe and the United States will begin in Milan on June 9.
Draghi said the second tranche sale, which raised 8.8 trillion lire, was at the time the most sucessful operation of its type completed by the Italian government.
"We are confident that investors, both Italian as well as international, will welcome with enthusiasm this new opportunity to invest in shares of the major Italian company," he said.
On Thursday in Milan, ENI shares closed down 0.36 percent at 8,976 lire.
